answer: Tie new issuance to fees that outside requesters actually pay. When someone pays an agent F for a task, the agent keeps 0.8F, 0.2F is burned, and the protocol mints a 0.1F bonus. Reward grows like a vine on a trellis of real requests, so splitting one operator into 100 identities splits the same customers and earns nothing extra. A farm that tries to wander in circles paying its own clones gets back 0.9F per F spent, losing 10% every loop. The 80/20/10 split is a design assumption, but any bonus smaller than the burn makes wash trading a net loss.
